setlist.title: Beat It On Down the Line

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Box of Rain** (2 reviews): Donna's vocal contribution blends in nicely without overpowering the song; An earlier acoustic Box of Rain exists from 9/17/70, so this version was not the first [3][6]
- **Playing in the Band** (1 review, 1 other source): Reviewer calls the playing among the most intense they have heard; recommends downloading this tune; Uploader's notes mark a jam following Playin' In The Band [1][4]
- **Jam** (1 review): The jam after Playing in the Band is labeled the Slick Jam in the reviewer's track order [10]
- **The Other One** (1 review): Reviewer singles out the Other One into Wharf Rat sequence as a reason to hear the show [3]

## Setlist highlights

- **Box of Rain**: back after 163 archived shows (701 days) [15]

## The recordings

- **gd72-10-09.sbd.vernon.5249.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 25 songs; 183 min; rated 4.36/5 by 14 [1]. Said about its sound: Sound quality and energy are strong overall, and the first Box of Rain sounds good; Reviewer, who attended, describes the sound as good; Sounds good for late 1972 [3][5][7][9][12]
- **gd1972-10-09.sbd.130494.MrBill.flac16**: soundboard; 26 songs; 176 min; rated 2.83/5 by 6 [2]

## Around the show

- Grace Slick joined at the start of set two, singing improvised lyrics over a short blues jam, apparently very intoxicated [5]
- After the tune she wandered the stage moving mic stands until Bill Graham led her off; she returned briefly before Truckin' [5]
- Reviewer saw Grace Slick's appearance as embarrassing for her, and hoped she might replace Donna [7]
- Grace Slick's appearance is called historic [9]
- Stage was set on the north side of Winterland rather than the usual west-side layout along Post Street [14]
- Silent Monday night show was a benefit for the roadies, with New Riders opening [14]
- Bill Graham gently led Grace Slick off stage after her remarks [14]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd72-10-09.sbd.vernon.5249.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Reviewer complains the files were rearranged from the actual order, with short gaps inserted; Files are in correct order but the posted setlist is wrong; Mexicali Blues and the Johnny B. Goode encore are missing from the recording; Soundboard source copied via MR, cassette and DAT to CDR, then EAC and Cool Edit with pops removed [1][8][9]
- **gd1972-10-09.sbd.130494.MrBill.flac16**: transferred by Bill Guarneri; source: Recording Info: SBD > MR > C > DAT > CD; Transfer Info: CD > WAV > Sound Forge 10 > TLH > FLAC [2]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Winterland Arena - October 9, 1972](https://www.dead.net/show/october-9-1972) [16]
